# Risk model backtest [SYNTHETIC: a known-truth history from sample_data/generate_risk_panel.py, 220 invented customers]

Model settings version `2026-11-27.1`; renewals judged from 180 days out; events: churned, downsold.

Scored out of time: 352 renewals, 63 of them lost (base rate 17.9%), from 7356 snapshots (2024-11-04 to 2026-08-24). Each renewal is judged 150, 90, 30 days ahead (871 judgements). Intervals are 95%, from resampling whole customers.

Past renewals: 78 lost, 291 kept on record, 23 kept with no record (a contract ran on after the date), 0 unconfirmed.

| Method | AUC | 95% interval | Precision, top 10% | Recall, top 10% | Brier | Losses expected / seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| scorecard (100 - health) | 0.784 | 0.722 to 0.833 | 0.393 | 0.269 | - | - |
| expert prior (probability) | 0.782 | 0.719 to 0.832 | 0.379 | 0.260 | 0.111 | 144 / 127 |
| trained model (probability) | 0.776 | 0.714 to 0.827 | 0.373 | 0.255 | 0.112 | 145 / 127 |
| scorecard without the CSM view (100 - health) | 0.787 | 0.726 to 0.835 | 0.448 | 0.307 | - | - |

Trained model minus expert prior, AUC: -0.013 to 0.002 (95% interval). The trained model is worth adopting only when this interval sits above zero and its Brier score is lower.

**Without the CSM's own view** (rating and register blanked) the scorecard ranks at AUC 0.787, against 0.784 with it. A CSM often rates a customer red AFTER it has said it is leaving. If the figure with the CSM's view is much the higher of the two, part of that is hindsight, not warning.

**The rules alone** (a hard red or health under 50) flag 0.135 of judgements, with precision 0.381 and recall 0.354 (AUC 0.628).

**Only the periods where the model had learned something** (716 judgements, 101 lost): AUC 0.764 against the prior's 0.764; Brier 0.112 against 0.110.

Retrainings by stage: prior 3, calibrated 12, dimension 9. The last one had 73 renewals lost to learn from.
